options.label: Three-quarter portrait
options.description: Close three-quarter head with black-to-charcoal background; AI treatment with the original available for comparison.
options.credit: Michelangelo / Galleria dell’Accademia; photograph published by Web Gallery of Art, photographer uncredited.
options.altText: Three-quarter portrait of David’s head, neck and sling-holding hand against a dark background.
options.license: Photographic reuse terms not established; app clearance pending.
options.sourceNotes: Original Accademia sculpture. A close photographic view, distinct from B and C. The background was replaced and the portrait reframed using the built-in image generator.
options.fidelityNotes: Broad face identity, pose, gaze and hand position remain recognizable. Fine marble speckling and hair texture are regenerated, so this is not pixel-preserving or a conservation reference. Compare the source before approving.
options.generationPrompt: Precise sculpture photograph edit. Image 1 is an authentic photograph of Michelangelo's original David in the Accademia, Florence. Image 2 provides BACKGROUND STYLE ONLY. Keep image 1's exact photographed head, neck, sling and visible shoulder/hand. Keep the same three-quarter camera view, expression, eye direction, hair carving, marble color, weathering, face proportions and lighting. Replace the architectural background only with near-black at the top, grading very subtly to charcoal toward the bottom like image 2. Compose a close head-and-shoulder portrait in a 4:5 frame; add approximately 15% black headroom by extending BACKGROUND ONLY, no new sculpture. Keep existing foreground intact and crop only at the lower edge if needed. Do not invent a new camera elevation, rotate or reshape the head, beautify, repair damage, sharpen by adding texture, invent hidden surfaces or borrow features from Caracalla. No text or watermark.

options.label: Frontal head
options.description: Native close photograph with a dark gallery background and direct view of the face.
options.credit: Michelangelo / Galleria dell’Accademia; photograph published by Web Gallery of Art, photographer uncredited.
options.altText: David’s face seen nearly frontally, with carved curls and his sling-holding hand at the lower left.
options.license: Photographic reuse terms not established; app clearance pending.
options.sourceNotes: Unaltered photograph of the Accademia original from a different viewing position than A. Existing warmer rendering and faint architectural lines remain. It is not color-matched or sharpened.
options.fidelityNotes: Native pixels preserved. The source is limited to 800 pixels wide and has little top headroom.

options.label: Head and shoulders
options.description: A separate photograph shows the head, shoulders and sling from a slightly lower viewpoint.
options.credit: Jörg Bittner Unna / Michelangelo, Galleria dell’Accademia.
options.altText: A photographic detail of David’s head, shoulders and raised left hand, with the museum wall behind.
options.license: CC BY 3.0 as stated on Wikimedia Commons; app use still pending review.
options.sourceNotes: Independent photograph of the Accademia original dated 21 July 2021. The unchanged full source is retained; the review thumbnail selects the head and shoulders. Genuine mildly upward perspective and pale architectural background remain.
options.fidelityNotes: Native pixels preserved. The displayed portrait is a crop of a wider photograph, not a new viewpoint. It does not meet the dark-background direction. The source was rejected by the image generator as an invalid image file; no repair or alternative-view synthesis was used.

options.label: Historical paired portrait
options.description: Both faces and transforming arms in a newly framed monochrome archive photograph.
options.credit: ICCD, Fondo Ferro Candilera, FFC009358; Gian Lorenzo Bernini, Galleria Borghese.
options.altText: Black-and-white upper-figure detail of Apollo and Daphne against the photograph’s black background.
options.license: ICCD publication authorization not established; review only.
options.sourceNotes: ICCD dates the photograph to 1920–1930. Full archive sheet retained, with border and catalogue lettering outside the thumbnail window. This is a newly sourced historical photograph, not a generated image.
options.fidelityNotes: Unchanged native photograph. Grain and archive print softness remain. Camera angle is preserved.

options.label: Daphne · close portrait
options.description: A tighter color portrait brings Daphne’s expression and carved hair forward.
options.credit: Galleria Borghese catalogue photograph; Gian Lorenzo Bernini.
options.altText: Close detail of Daphne’s head, hair and raised arm against black.
options.license: Museum photographic reuse not established; review only.
options.sourceNotes: New close detail from the unchanged official photograph used earlier. The same source is deliberately reframed on Daphne rather than the whole sculptural pair. Not represented as a new photograph.
options.fidelityNotes: Native pixels and real camera view preserved. The tighter crop excludes Apollo and part of the raised leaves; the full original is available.

options.label: Apollo · close portrait
options.description: A separate close framing of Apollo’s face, curls and upper chest.
options.credit: Galleria Borghese catalogue photograph; Gian Lorenzo Bernini.
options.altText: Apollo’s face and upper chest, with a small portion of Daphne at the right, against black.
options.license: Museum photographic reuse not established; review only.
options.sourceNotes: Another framing of the unchanged official photograph. This option emphasizes Apollo rather than Daphne or the pair. B and C are two composition choices from the same photograph, not independent sources.
options.fidelityNotes: Native sculpture pixels, lighting and camera view preserved. No AI or editing. The right edge includes part of Daphne where she is adjacent to Apollo in the original.
